noveltyJustification: All four findings are new because no prior lineage read these four packages; two establish no-candidate verdicts and two identify answer-dependent gates.
keyQuestions: Which scenarios in the 28 unaudited packages meet Q2 or Q3 and should convert or gain a conversation companion, and which are blocked by the runner's five runtimes and three session actions?
Which existing single-prompt scenarios need updating rather than converting because the behavior is multi-turn but the current scenario checks it only once?
Which packages have no conversation candidate at all, so every scenario stays single prompt under Q1 or Q4?
Which multi-turn, answer-dependent, restart, compaction or cross-runtime behaviors in these packages lack any scenario that a conversation would add?
Which candidates rank highest by risk reduction relative to authoring and run cost across the 28 packages?
ruledOut: Converting SD-007 itself into a conversation
Treating SKD-022 as an approval gate

label: sk-code-skilled has no conversation candidate: its twelve scenarios are routing-recall contracts where one prompt must emit one intent's resource set, plus the shared tier and surface-detection checks; OC-008 runs guards but reads their exit statuses in one pass, so Q2 finds no second exchange and Q4 keeps them single prompt.

The sk-design hub keeps SD-005, SD-H05 and SD-H10 single prompt as routing traces (Q4), but SD-007 is an add candidate: its contract allows the router to explicitly ask the user to disambiguate, citing both candidate intents and their scores, and no turn scripts the answer that would then select CHART or FLOWCHART (Q2). Add a companion conversation rather than convert the routing-gold file.

sk-design-diagram keeps eight of ten scenarios single prompt (Q1 for the judged DIA-002 and CAP-001, Q4 for the rest), but DIA-003 needs updating to a conversation: its contract makes the approval halt load-bearing, says style-guide.md changes only after explicit approval, and instructs the agent to stop and wait, so a two-turn script that approves or declines is the only way a shell check can observe the write decision (Q2).

sk-design-fundamentals has no conversation candidate: its twelve scenarios are one-prompt routing, value-scale, conflict and boundary checks, and SKD-022 expects the agent to choose the shadow system from how much work shadows do in the project rather than to ask the operator, so Q2 does not apply and Q4 keeps them single prompt.

direction: Converting SD-007 itself into a conversation
reason: It is a routing-gold file whose YAML contract and expected resources feed the typed-gold gate; a companion operator scenario keeps that gate intact while adding the answer turn.

direction: Treating SKD-022 as an approval gate
reason: The reference tells the agent to choose the shadow system from the project's needs, not to ask the operator.
